rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣaff and al-Jumu‘ah share a central theme, though their styles and arguments differ.
rows.anchor: Only the style and arguments of both are different.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding sūrah recalls Jesus’ prediction about Muhammad; al-Jumu‘ah alludes to Abraham’s prayer for the Ishmaelites.
rows.anchor: This sūrah alludes to the prayer of Abraham

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ishmaelites must honour God’s favor of sending Muhammad among them and resist Jewish conspiracies that could deprive them of it.
rows.anchor: and to not deprive themselves of this great blessing by being misled by the conspiracies of the Jews.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preferring trade to Friday prayer and the Prophet’s sermon shows Muslims have not understood their bargain with God described in the preceding sūrah.
rows.anchor: then this only means that they have not understood the deal of sale and purchase they have struck with their Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims are warned against repeating the Jews’ disregard, which cost them God’s sharī‘ah; they should not follow their example.
rows.anchor: the Jews had adopted the same behavior, and, as a result were deprived of the sharī‘ah of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Business and trade activities must not make Muslims indifferent to God and His Prophet.
rows.anchor: should make him indifferent to God and His Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This repeats the Jews’ error concerning the Sabbath; the Almighty cursed them, and Muslims had already been forbidden to follow their path.
rows.anchor: The Jews had erred similarly in the matter of sabt, and the Almighty, as result, had severely cursed them for this attitude.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recurring opening uses the present tense here, unlike the preceding sūrah’s past tense, to portray the glorification as occurring before the eyes.
rows.anchor: which brings the portrayal before the eyes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four divine attributes in the opening serve as a preamble to the account of the Messenger in verse 2.
rows.anchor: The verse mentions four attributes of God; all these attributes come as a preamble to the succeeding verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is sent to manifest God’s attributes: as Sovereign, God informs creation of His directives through a Messenger who recites His teachings and guidance.
rows.anchor: the Messenger mentioned in this verse was sent forth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is pure and flawless, He sent His Messenger and teachings to purify people’s beliefs and deeds and cleanse moral evils.
rows.anchor: He is pure and flawless, and for this reason He wanted to purify people through His Messenger and His teachings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kitāb means sharī‘ah or divine law, whose enforcement requires power and authority; God’s wisdom makes that law express people’s welfare in this life and the next, not force alone.
rows.anchor: The word al-kitāb here means the sharī‘ah or the divine law. The sharī‘ah can only be enforced by someone who is powerful and has authority.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The designation “unlettered” distinguishes the Ishmaelites; Islahi says Jews coined it to express religious arrogance and derision toward Arabia’s people.
rows.anchor: this term was actually coined specifically by the Jews among the People of the Book which reflected their religious arrogance as well as derision for the people of Arabia

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though unfamiliar with divine law, the Ishmaelites adopted “unlettered” as a title without inferiority; Qur’anic use raised it into a mark of divinely given respect.
rows.anchor: they themselves adopted this term as a title without any inferiority complex

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s providence reversed the status of a people once disparaged: they were entrusted with guiding the whole world.
rows.anchor: they, who were derided and disparaged were entrusted with the responsibility of instructing and guiding the whole world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those proud to possess a divine book and sharī‘ah are likened to a donkey carrying books.
rows.anchor: they who felt pride in being the recipient of a divine book and sharī‘ah were compared to a donkey that is laden with books

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The designation also stirs gratitude: God sent a person from among the Ishmaelites to reform and educate them in law and wisdom, lifting them from jāhiliyyah.
rows.anchor: For their own reformation and instruction and to educate them in law and wisdom, He sent forth among them a person from among themselves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipients should value and honour this favour and encourage others to do likewise, lest they lose it and vindicate the envious.
rows.anchor: they who have received this favour should value and honour it, and also try that others adopt this attitude as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi directs readers to his earlier Baqarah discussion of the unlettered Prophet’s attributes to address rejecters of Hadith who misunderstand his mission.
rows.anchor: Readers are advised to look it up so that the misunderstandings which have been spread by the rejecters of Ḥadīth regarding the purpose of his advent are dispelled.

words: وَيَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham prayed for an Ishmaelite messenger with the same tasks named in 62:2: reciting revelation, teaching law and wisdom, and purifying the people.
rows.anchor: Abraham (sws) had prayed to God to send forth a prophet among the Ishmaelites having exactly these attributes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad manifests both God’s attributes and Abraham’s prayer, and combines several distinct attributes.
rows.anchor: just as Muḥammad (sws) is a manifestation of the attributes of God, he is also a manifestation of the prayer of Abraham (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad fulfills Jesus’ prediction and Abraham’s prayer while reflecting God’s attributes as a human being from among the unlettered Arabs.
rows.anchor: He is the realization of Jesus’ prediction and the manifestation of Abraham’s prayer. He is also a reflection of God’s attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Messenger was no alien to the Arabs, their detractors cannot claim they received guidance through another people; God elevated them to carry guidance to the world.
rows.anchor: He is no stranger or alien to them. Those who are belittling them cannot blame them that they received the light of guidance through them or through some other means

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s specific mission to the Ishmaelites was completed by him; his universal mission to humanity continues through his followers, witnesses to truth until Judgment, with the Ishmaelites as vanguard.
rows.anchor: The former related to the Ishmaelites and the obligations of this prophethood were brought a completion by the Prophet (sws) himself. The latter related to all mankind

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about their former manifest error recalls the people’s long ignorance so they recognize God’s favour in bringing them from darkness to honour.
rows.anchor: are meant to stir up feelings of gratitude in the ummiyyīn. They had been engulfed in darkness of ignorance since a long time.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 3 is grammatically coordinated with “ummiyyīn” in verse 2, and refers to others yet to join the community addressed by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: This verse is coordinated to the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although “ummiyyīn” is general in wording, Islahi reads verse 2 as referring specifically to Ishmaelites who had already embraced faith; its closing clause that they were previously in manifest error supports this.
rows.anchor: in the previous verse though the word ummiyyīn is used in the general sense, it referred to only those Ishmaelites who had already embraced faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among them” signals that some Ishmaelites who are foremost recipients of the favour still resist the call, and tactfully urges them to accept faith.
rows.anchor: among these ummiyyīn who are the recipient of this divine favour, there are others who are as yet averse to this call

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase contains glad tidings that those not yet among the believers will soon accept faith and join them.
rows.anchor: though at the moment these people have not joined the ranks of the believers, they soon will
